title: String and array boundary errors; avoiding buffer overflows (CodeSaathi extension)

understand.concept: A buffer overflow occurs when a program reads or writes outside the intended bounds of an array or buffer. Common causes include incorrect length calculations, missing terminators, off-by-one loops and unsafe input handling.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Out-of-bounds access is undefined behaviour in C and can cause crashes, data corruption or security vulnerabilities. Correctness requires validating lengths before every write and read.

practise.guidedTask: The required size includes the null terminator. The copy occurs only after checking that the destination has enough bytes.
